First attempt on a #TidyTuesday dataviz. This week the data are [historic UK meteorological and climate data from the UK Met Office](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2025/2025-10-21). As a resident in western Norway I am obliged to make some plot about rain ☔️...

<!-- ![](TT-2025-42.png){width=75% fig-align="center"} -->

```{r libraries, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytuesdayR)
```

```{r data, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2025, week = 42)

historic_station_met <- tuesdata$historic_station_met
station_meta <- tuesdata$station_meta
```

## Exploration

Want to make a simple plot of location of the stations from the station_metadata

```{r exploration, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
glimpse(station_meta)
```

Trying to see the spread of the stations opened before 1925, so that there will be 100 years of data (1924-2024). 

```{r plot-1, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, dpi=300, dev='png'}
old_stations <- station_meta |> 
    filter(opened < 1925)

ggplot(station_meta) +
    geom_point(aes(x = lng, y = lat), color = "blue", size = 1) +
    geom_point(data=old_stations, aes(x = lng, y = lat), color = "red", size = 1) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(title = "UK Meteorological Stations opened before 1925",
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude")
```

They seem to be fairly evenly spread across the UK.

Names of the 10 stations, in a table from oldest to newest: 

```{r table-1}
old_stations |> 
    select(station_name, opened) |>
    arrange(opened) |>
    knitr::kable()
```

## Wrangling

- There are 10 stations opened before 1925. 
- Maybe a time series annual for all of them, and then facet them by station? 
- one line per year (x - month, y - percepitation). Maybe highlight the 1924 and 2024 lines? (gghighlight?)

```{r wrangling, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
old_station_ids <- old_stations$station

old_station_data <- historic_station_met |> 
    filter(station %in% old_station_ids, year >= 1924) |> 
    left_join(old_stations |> select(station, station_name), by="station")

glimpse(old_station_data)
```

finne snittdata

```{r}
# calculate average per month per station in the period. 
average_station_data <- old_station_data |> 
    group_by(station, station_name, month) |> 
    summarise(avg_rain = mean(rain, na.rm=TRUE)) |> 
    ungroup()

average_station_data
```

## Plotting



```{r plot-3, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, dpi=300, dev='png'}
# plot average line per station
ggplot(average_station_data) +
    geom_line(aes(x = month, y = avg_rain, group = station_name, color=station_name), size = 1) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
    #facet_wrap(~station_name, ncol=5) +
    labs(title = "Average Monthly Precipitation at UK Meteorological Stations opened before 1925",
         x = "Month",
         y = "Precipitation (mm)") +
    theme(
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    )

```


```{r plot-2, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, dpi=300, dev='png'}
ggplot(old_station_data) +
    geom_line(aes(x = month, y = rain, group = year, color = year), alpha = 0.1) +
    #geom_line(data = old_station_data |> filter(year == 1924), 
    #          aes(x = month, y = rain), color = "blue", size = 1) +
    #geom_line(data = old_station_data |> filter(year == 2024), 
    #          aes(x = month, y = rain), color = "red", size = 1    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
    facet_wrap(~station_name, ncol=5) +
    labs(title = "Monthly Precipitation at UK Meteorological Stations opened before 1925",
         subtitle = "Grey lines are years 1925-2023, blue is 1924, red is 2024",
         x = "Month",
         y = "Precipitation (mm)") +
    theme(
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    )
```
